crossRefs.note: Even to this present hour we hunger, thirst, are naked, are beaten, and have no certain dwelling place.
in labor and travail, in watchings often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, and in cold and nakedness.
Passing by Mysia, they came down to Troas.
Setting sail therefore from Troas, we made a straight course to Samothrace, and the day following to Neapolis;
But these had gone ahead, and were waiting for us at Troas.

people.name: Troas
people.line: A city in Asia Minor, visited by Paul

translations.web: Bring the cloak that I left at Troas with Carpus when you come, and the books, especially the parchments.
translations.bsb: When you come, bring the cloak that I left with Carpus at Troas, and my scrolls, especially the parchments.
translations.kjv: The cloke that I left at Troas with Carpus, when thou comest, bring with thee, and the books, but especially the parchments.
translations.asv: The cloak that I left at Troas with Carpus, bring when thou comest, and the books, especially the parchments.
